text:
Maria: Heads-up — Vendor (AeroLink) just sent a revised invoice for PO#89234 (H100 replacements). Exchange rate reval added ~7% on parts and a passthrough FX fee. This pushes the RMA freight + customs estimate up by ~€18k. Need finance signoff before we approve AWB.
Kai: Can you post the delta numbers? rough line items pls.
Maria: Sure — copying the vendor summary: ```parts_orig: $1,200,000; parts_adj_fx: +$84,000; vendor_fx_fee: $6,300; rma_freight_air: $12,400 -> new est: $30,700 (air+customs+broker)```
Tomas: Oof. Is that for full batch replacements or just DOA subset?
Maria: It's for the 14 DOA units + 6 partial swaps (total 20). Vendor split the invoice across replacement SKU and RMA logistics lines.
Priya: If we switch non-urgent replacements to sea (LCL) we can drop freight by ~60% but lead time goes +10–14 days. Do we have spare pool coverage to avoid outages?
Kai: EU dedicated pool has 3 N+ spare H100s reserved; extra capacity is tight in APAC but EU can cover 10 of the 20 for a two-week window.
Lena (Finance): We need a clear cost-owner decision. Is vendor willing to absorb FX movement for RMA items under warranty? Vendor email says they only absorb manufacturing cost, not FX reval.
Maria: Exactly — vendor position is warranty covers replacement units but not currency swings or expedited freight. They offered to split expedite cost 50/50 for air if we accept consolidated AWB.
Tomas: Can we ask them to consolidate AWBs to avoid extra brokerage/HS code noise? Single AWB + split manifest avoids repeated customs entries.
Kai: Consolidation helps but customs still charges per line for duties. If vendor re-invoices in EUR vs USD that would neutralize exchange exposure — did they provide EUR invoice option?
Maria: They offered USD only due to their treasury hedging. I asked for EUR invoicing but no firm commitment yet.
Priya: Operational tradeoff: Option A = accept vendor 50/50 expedite share, air now, get replacements in 72h, cost +€9k to us. Option B = use dedicated spares for immediate coverage + sea for 10 replacements, vendor bills USD & we absorb FX on parts (~€84k) but avoid air freight spike. Option C = demand vendor credit for FX on warranty items (low chance).
Lena (Finance): Finance can cover one-time expedite up to €10k from contingency. Anything above needs director approval.
Kai: For logistics, if we go with Option A we should: 1) request consolidated AWB and HS harmonization, 2) insist on vendor-provided depot photos on handoff, 3) route half the units via our preferred forwarder (NordSea) to keep broker fees predictable.
Maria: Noted. Vendor asked for sign-off by EOD to meet their carrier cut. I pinged their account manager: "we can accept 50/50 expedite if you consolidate AWBs and waive the FX fee for the rma_freight line". Waiting reply.
OpsBot: Incident: eu-edge-03 reported 2 degraded nodes due to DOA H100s at 12:04 UTC; remediation ticket INF-4721 created.
Tomas: If infra can shift workload to eu-edge-04 and eu-edge-08 we can avoid customer impact for 48h. Ops, can you confirm scheduling?
Kai: Yes—we'll patch capacity from the spares pool overnight. Need confirmation from SRE on canary traffic shift.
Priya: If vendor refuses consolidation, we push them to use our broker under DDP terms and invoice vendor for broker fees. Should escalate to vendor-relations.
Maria: Vendor replied: "we can consolidate AWBs but cannot waive FX fee. We can invoice EUR for next PO only." They offered a €4k credit vs the FX fee.
Lena (Finance): With vendor €4k credit + Finance expedite €10k, we can cover air option within €15k threshold. I'll approve up to €10k now. Maria, can you capture approvals in the PO amendment?
Maria: Will do. Action items: @Kai consolidate AWB routing (NordSea preferred for half); @Priya coordinate spare-pool moves for 10 units; @Tomas notify SRE for canary shift; @Lena finalize contingency approval. I’ll circulate PO amendment and request vendor to release consolidated AWB by EOD.
Kai: On it, creating shipping instruction and sharing AWB draft in #vendors-shipping once ready.
Tomas: Noted — SRE will hold canary cutoff window 02:00–04:00 UTC tomorrow.
Priya: I'll hold sea-booking quotes as backup (LCL ETA +12d) in case vendor stalls.
Maria: Thanks all — tagging @vendor-relations to follow up escalation if vendor backtracks. :thumbsup:
